frames.prompt: Single animation keyframe, not a grid. Use this gray mannequin/teal shorts/low posterior shoulder bar position as reference. Show him STANDING at the start of a low-bar squat, knees straight but not hyperextended, hips extended, torso slightly forward to balance low bar above midfoot. Same rear three-quarter camera and same barbell. Full body framed with generous margins: entire character from head to shoes inside central 65 percent of a square canvas, entire bar within central 80 percent. Shoes firmly planted, shoulder-width, rear view left shoe at x=43% bottom y=83%, right shoe at x=59% bottom y=86%. Plain opaque uniform light gray background. Head must have plenty of space above. Both hands wrap bar just outside shoulders, shaft clearly across back of deltoids BELOW top of shoulders, not neck. One person, one bar, no text no rack. This will be fixed-camera frame 1 of sixteen.

Create ONE intermediate animation frame between reference image1 STANDING and image2 BOTTOM SQUAT. This frame is 1/15 (6.67%) of descent from image1 toward image2. Body only begins to bend knees and move hips slightly backward/down. Bar center moves about 18 pixels downward from image1 (on a 1254px canvas), not halfway down. Preserve exact image1 camera, canvas, background, body proportions and BOTH SHOES pixel-for-pixel: fixed floor positions, orientation and size. Bar length/plates/grip unchanged; bar remains supported on posterior shoulders. Keep same gray character teal shorts. No recentering, no cropping, no zoom, no new objects. Render only this single early-descent pose, square image.

Make the tiniest possible next-frame edit: keep this full-body pose almost identical but bend knees 2 degrees more and lower bar/shoulders by just 8 pixels. Do NOT make a quarter squat. Keep shoe pixels, camera, scale, equipment and entire gray background unchanged. Single low bar squat animation frame, gray man teal shorts.

Precise subtle pose edit of this single frame. Lower the shoulders, hands and entire barbell by ONLY about 20 pixels (1.6 percent of full image height), and hips by a similarly small amount, by bending both knees just a little more. This is the NEXT animation frame, so the change must be tiny, NOT a half squat. Keep both shoes exactly unchanged and fixed to same pixels. Keep same anatomy, equipment, camera, image dimensions, background, scale, low-bar shoulder contact, and grip. No zoom or recentering. Return one frame.

One animation in-between pose exactly halfway between these two shallow squat frames. Interpolate head, bar, shoulders, hips and knee bend halfway. Preserve exact shoes, canvas, camera, background, equipment scale and grip. Very shallow low-bar squat, NOT a deep squat. Gray mannequin teal shorts. No zoom, recentering or cropping. Single frame only.

ONE intermediate low-bar squat animation frame. Image1 is fixed STANDING reference; image2 is BOTTOM reference. Frame 4 of16: 3/15 descent (20%). Bar shaft center at y=336 on the 1254px square canvas. Hips descend gradually, knees bend, neutral spine and slight forward torso lean increasing with depth. Preserve image1 BOTH SHOES pixel-for-pixel, exact size, positions, orientation. Preserve camera, canvas, framing, equipment dimensions, grip, gray character teal shorts and plain gray background. NO zoom, NO recentering. Bar stays across rear deltoids; hands attached. Single full body pose, not grid. Only body above ankles changes to requested intermediate depth, never bottom yet.

Moderately bend hips and knees, hips backward/down; neutral spine, low bar across rear deltoids and firm grip. Target bar shaft around 390px from top of 1254px image. Edit ONLY pose above the ankles: make this same person descend to bottom of a LOW BAR squat, thighs parallel to ground, hips back, torso inclined forward with neutral spine and bar over midfoot. Preserve BOTH SHOES and their positions PIXEL-FOR-PIXEL; do not move, resize or rotate the feet. Preserve exact camera, canvas, background, character size, bar length, plates, grip spacing. No recentering or zoom. The bar stays in contact with rear deltoids below tops of shoulders. Head, shoulders, bar and hips move downward naturally, knees bend outward in line with toes.
